summary: Elevated first-token latency and intermittent streaming timeouts for chat completions after scheduler tuning
description: Issue summary: BrightHealth AI reports a spike in time-to-first-token (TTFB) for chat completions with occasional streaming disconnects after a scheduler parameter tuning that rolled out on 2026-03-09. Impact: Affected customer (dedicated) is experiencing degraded UX for interactive chat flows: median TTFB increased from ~120ms to ~900ms for short prompts, and ~10% of streaming sessions hit client-observed timeouts (30s) before first token. Production impact is customer-visible; business-critical for the customer's in-product chat feature. Environment: Production (dedicated pool) in us-east. Recent changes: scheduler tuning (session-placement affinity / bin-packing thresholds) + runtime microkernel scheduler patch (PRs linked).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Use BrightHealth AI org credentials to create a chat completion request with streaming enabled against the dedicated endpoint in us-east.
2) Send a short user prompt (<50 tokens) with model pinned to redwood-chat-3b-quant.
3) Observe initial latency until first token and any streaming disconnects.
4) Repeat across ~100 requests to reproduce elevated median TTFB and intermittent timeouts.
Note: Issue is intermittent — amplify by running parallel clients at 20-40rps to match customer traffic pattern.
observed_behavior:
- Median TTFB increased from ~120ms (baseline) to ~900ms for short prompts.
- ~10% of streaming sessions fail to receive first token within 30s (client timeout).
- 5xx errors were not consistently present; many requests completed successfully but with long stall before initial token.
- Spike correlates with times of scheduler rebalancing and when new GPU workers join the pool.
expected_behavior: Median TTFB should remain close to historical baseline (<250ms for short prompts) and streaming should deliver first token within the customer's client timeout window.
logs:
Representative logs attached (obfuscated):
- api-gateway request IDs: rQk-9a1, rQk-9a2, rQk-9a7 show 28s stall before first token.
- serving-runtime traces: long wait in `kv_cache_lookup` + `worker-queue-wait` for requests routed to node gpu-12.
- scheduler logs: rebalance cycle triggered and moved 18 sessions at 2026-03-09T22:14:03Z.
- nginx upstream times do not indicate client-level network stalls.
(Full logs uploaded to attached artifacts: s3://support-artifacts/SUP-17583/)
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: scheduler tuning changed session placement causing some requests to queue behind heavy priming work on newly provisioned GPUs.
Repro attempt in staging with identical scheduler flags reproduced median TTFB increase when simulated priming traffic present.
Tracing shows increased `worker-queue` latency specifically when requests land on nodes that recently received large KV cache loads (priming / prefix caching).
Correlation observed between rebalance events (scheduler) and TTFB spikes; nodes that accepted moved sessions show transient high queue times for ~30-90s after rebalance.
No widespread memory pressure or GPU OOMs found. CPU utilization on affected nodes spikes during rebalance window (related to cache materialization).
Potential secondary cause: runtime microkernel changed scheduling quantum causing fewer background cache materialization threads — prolonging priming time.
Customer-side telemetry: traffic pattern includes bursts of short interactive sessions which are sensitive to first-token latency.
customer_communications: 2026-03-10T10:12 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledge receipt, requested logs and sample request IDs; informed customer we're investigating and provided ETA for first update (2h).
2026-03-10T12:40 - Customer (BrightHealth AI): Confirmed elevated TTFB across multiple users; provided request IDs and noted user timeout observed in mobile app.
engineer_comments: 2026-03-10T15:02 - Jared Kim (SRE): Reproduced in pre-prod when enabling 'aggressive-bin-pack' scheduler flag. Observed same worker-queue wait pattern. Rolling back flag in pre-prod reverted TTFB to baseline.

2026-03-11T09:18 - Lina Torres (Runtime): Microkernel runtime change in PR #621 reduces concurrency for background KV materialization by default. We saw increased cold-cache priming time. Working on a patch to allow opportunistic materialization threads during rebalance.
2026-03-12T08:05 - Ops: Temporary mitigation deployed — throttle rebalance frequency and prefer warm-hosts; monitoring for regressions.
temporary_workaround: Rolled back aggressive bin-packing scheduler flag on the customer's dedicated pool and applied a conservative rebalance cooldown (60s). Additionally re-enabled opportunistic cache materialization setting on affected runtime nodes. These mitigations reduced median TTFB back toward baseline in canary tests.
root_cause: Scheduler rebalance interaction with recent runtime microkernel change: rebalance moved sessions to nodes that required KV/prefix cache materialization while runtime deprioritized background cache work, causing a window where new requests queued behind cache warm-up and increased first-token latency.
resolution_plan:
1) Patch runtime (PR incoming) to restore opportunistic KV materialization threads during rebalance.
2) Revert aggressive scheduler bin-packing by default; introduce rollout gate and per-customer opt-in.
3) Add instrumentation to detect rebalance-induced cache-warm windows and auto-warm hot keys for moved sessions.
4) Postmortem and update runbook for rebalance + cache interactions.
Timeline: hotfix applied to customer's pool (done). Runtime patch targeted for 2026-03-15, scheduler default rollback targeted for 2026-03-16.
resolution_notes: Hotfix (scheduler cooldown + cache materialization toggle) applied to BrightHealth AI dedicated pool on 2026-03-11; customer confirmed marked improvement in TTFB by 2026-03-12. Follow-up runtime patch queued and slated for patch release. Postmortem will be published to Confluence after release.
